introduction: As science advanced, physicists began to look inside the atom and decipher the invisible relationship between electricity and magnetism. This level covers the revolutions of the 19th and early 20th centuries.

core_concepts.title: Discovery of Subatomic Particles (E, P, N)
core_concepts.description:
1. Electron ($e^-$): J.J. Thomson (1897). 
2. Proton ($p^+$): Ernest Rutherford (1920). (Note: Eugen Goldstein discovered canal rays, but Rutherford named the proton and proved its existence in the nucleus). 
3. Neutron ($n^0$): James Chadwick (1932).

core_concepts.title: Radioactivity
core_concepts.description:
Discoverer: Henri Becquerel (1896). 
Later, Marie Curie and Pierre Curie discovered highly radioactive elements like 'Radium' and 'Polonium'. Marie Curie is the only woman to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields (Physics and Chemistry).

core_concepts.title: Dynamo and Electromagnetic Induction (EMI)
core_concepts.description:
Discoverer: Michael Faraday (1831). 
Faraday proved that moving a magnet near a wire generates electricity. Every major power plant in the world today runs on this principle. He is known as the 'Father of Electricity'.

core_concepts.title: Electric Battery
core_concepts.description:
Inventor: Alessandro Volta (1800). 
He invented the first electrical battery (the voltaic pile). The unit of electrical potential, the 'Volt', is named in his honor.

important_entities.name: Television
important_entities.significance: The Television was invented by John Logie Baird (J.L. Baird) in 1925. This is a very frequent question in RRB NTPC and Group D exams.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: In addition to the proton, it was 'Ernest Rutherford' who discovered the atomic 'Nucleus' through his famous Gold Foil Alpha-Scattering Experiment.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Just match the initials: P->R, E->T, N->C.

exam_strategy_tips: Frequently asked in State PCS exams: 'Who invented the Dynamo?' Answer: Michael Faraday.
